topic_title: Understand the characteristics of basic univariate distributions and how to generate samples from them
cmp_edition: IFoA CS1 Core Reading / CMP · 2026 syllabus alignment

mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to generate discrete and continuous random variables using statistical software. So software sampling is deliberate and checkable against the families and methods you already hold, without opening joint distributions.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to generate draws in software for basic discrete and continuous families and to sanity-check output (refusing both GUI theatre and silent claim that Chapter 2 is finished)
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from 'I know inverse transform' to 'I can obtain software-generated samples and check them honestly.'
mission.learning_objective: Generate discrete and continuous random variables using statistical software.
mission.concept_focus: Named family → software sampler → generate sample → sanity check against support/moments → refuse generation-without-check.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday's inverse transform is the method spine; today is Syllabus 2.1.6 software generation for the same univariate families.
mission.why_now: 2.1.6 completes the univariate generation pair after inverse transform; Revision follows before 2.2.
mission.expected_benefit: You will be able to generate a discrete and a continuous sample in software and run a sanity check that matches the family's support and mean.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Gamma Day 4 because it is the final Learning LO in 2.1 before Revision.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: software generation plan
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Name one discrete and one continuous family. For each, state what you would ask statistical software to generate and one sanity check you would run.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Software LO is deliberate generate + check, not menu tourism.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Example: Discrete (generate Poisson(λ) counts; check non-negative integers and sample mean near λ. Continuous) generate Exp(λ); check positive support and mean near 1/λ.
success_criteria: One sanity check each or shared clear checks.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: refuse Chapter 2 complete
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) For Poisson(λ=3) and Exponential(mean=2), state what you ask software to generate and one numeric sanity check for each (support and/or sample mean). (2) Refuse: 'Software generation replaces understanding the inverse-transform method' and 'finishing software generation means I already sanity-checked the sample.'
hints: 2.1 Learning may be complete after today + Revision.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Poisson(3): generate non-negative integer counts; check integers ≥0 and sample mean near 3. Exponential(mean 2): generate positive reals (rate 1/2); check support >0 and sample mean near 2. (2) Refuse: a sampler is not a substitute for knowing how inverse-transform sampling works; generating alone is not a sanity check. You must verify support and moments against the named family.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating a software sampler as finished without a support/moment sanity check, or equating generation with inverse-transform understanding.
